core_obligations: Represent E by a K-injective complex with injective terms so that the four derived pushforwards are computed by pushforwards of the complex and its restrictions (proof lines 8267-8274).
Identify the sought triangle with the one attached to the displayed short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves on Y (proof lines 8275-8287).

Establish exactness of that sequence using the relative Mayer-Vietoris lemma and the vanishing of the first higher direct image of an injective module, and deduce functoriality in E from the functoriality of the K-injective construction (proof lines 8288-8294).
proof_roadmap: Triangle from a short exact sequence of complexes (proof lines 8275-8287).
Exactness via relative Mayer-Vietoris and functoriality (proof lines 8288-8294).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of ringed spaces f: X to Y with X the union of two open subsets, the lemma produces a distinguished triangle relating the derived pushforward of an arbitrary object of the unbounded derived category to the derived pushforwards of its restrictions along the three restrictions of f, and asserts functoriality in the object (statement lines 8249-8264). The proof follows the same pattern as the absolute case: represent E by a K-injective complex with injective terms, so that the four derived pushforwards are computed by the corresponding pushforwards of the restricted complexes, and identify the triangle with the one attached to a short exact sequence of complexes of sheaves on Y (proof lines 8266-8287). Exactness of that sequence is now derived from the relative Mayer-Vietoris lemma together with the vanishing of the first higher direct image of an injective module, rather than termwise as in the absolute case (proof lines 8288-8291). Functoriality is inherited from the functoriality of the K-injective construction (proof lines 8292-8294). The claim is H2: the same reduction as the absolute case with a different exactness input, plus a short functoriality argument.
